summary: 1939 80-foot Aermotor steel fire tower on Lightning Peak, Bonner County, Idaho; listed as gone in 1953, and no source describes what remains.

facts.design: 80-foot Aermotor LX-24 steel tower with 7x7 cab
facts.status_note: Gone by 1953; no source describes what, if anything, remains at the peak

events.note: Lightning Creek lookout reported smoke blocking views of the Pack River and Upper Grouse Creek districts (Pend Oreille Review, quoted by Forest Lookouts)
80-foot Aermotor LX-24 steel tower with 7x7 cab

corrections.why: Three sources give an 80-foot steel tower for 1939 (about 24.4 m). The record's 21.3 m is 70 feet, the height of a 1933 tower at the Little Lightning creek station that the sources do not tie to this peak.

notes_for_editor: Height: the record's 21.3 m (70 ft) conflicts with 80 ft in three sources; the 70-ft figure matches a 1933 tower at the Little Lightning creek station that the sources do not link to this peak. Record's 1953 'abandoned' is only 'Gone' in the sources, so it is recorded as other. Staffer name is spelled as the Idaho site prints it (Garreth Rouse); not checked against the 1949 Herald. One web search found no independent source for this tower. No site-today source found.
